instruction.text: Select the image that matches the Roman practice that continued in Britain after AD 410.

atoms.b: The Britons continued to trade with the Roman Empire, ((++buying breaking)) pottery, olive oil and wine. Many of Britain’s ((++roads toads)) today still follow the ancient Roman routes.
Britons also continued to practise Christianity and ((++use eat)) Latin for important writing.

instruction.text: Select the person who you think might still have been writing during the Dark Ages.

feedback.finish: After the Roman magistrates left, the only people in Britain who could read or write were members of the Church, such as monks.

atoms.a: Why do you think monks were the only people writing in Britain?
b: ++The Church taught them to read and write so they could study the Bible.
They were the only people who could afford pens.
They were born with the ability to read and write.

hint.label: Monks
hint.text: A monk is a man living away from the outside world in a religious community. They were the most educated men in Britain.

instruction.text: What do you think monks wrote with? Select the two correct answers.
Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Two of the most important Christian monks writing about Britain were called Gildas and the Venerable Bede.
Gildas was born in around AD 500, so he was writing over 100 years after the Romans had already left Britain.
Bede was writing another 200 years after that. However, he carefully checked various sources to make his work as accurate as possible.

hint.label: Source
hint.text: A source is a piece of information that we use to learn about history. It could be a book, a painting or another artefact.

atoms.a: How do you think their work would be affected by writing about events that happened before their time?
b: Their work would be more reliable.

atoms.a: Which writer do you think is more reliable?

feedback.correct: As Bede checked his sources, he was given the title “venerable”, which means well respected.
